downloadedSourceCountNote: Zero is correct and is the assignment's pinned value. Nothing was downloaded, no issuer was contacted, no file entered version control and no receipt was created. Every measurement below was taken from the bytes this repository already retains and which the adopted edition already manifests.

method.description: Deterministic in-repository identity reconciliation. The retained FEE102 binary was opened and measured, its printed footer and statutory citation were read from the face, and the result was compared against the adopted edition row, the repository asset audit, the source-acquisition queue and the three components that bind it. No network retrieval, no issuer contact, no legal-design change and no edition mutation were performed.
method.tooling: poppler (pdfinfo, pdftotext -layout) for face text and footer reads; pdf-lib for AcroForm, annotation and page-geometry reads
method.assignmentConstraintObserved: The stop condition confines this job to retained repository assets and deterministic identity mapping, with no download, no issuer contact, no legal-design change and no edition edit. Every finding is derived from retained bytes or retained records.

finding.headline: The document is present, correctly identified and byte-matched to the adopted edition. What is wrong is the class the edition assigns it: FEE102 is manifested as supporting_process, which the authority gate treats as unable to back an official-form component, and three fee_waiver components bind it. This is an edition reclass, exactly as the job name says, and no acquisition can fix it.
finding.acquisitionRequiredRationale: Nothing needs to be obtained from the Minnesota Judicial Branch. The binary is retained, digest-matched to the edition row, and its printed revision is legible on every page. No issuer interaction can change an asset class held in this repository.
finding.whyARemapCannotFixItEither: Rebinding the three components to any other retained Minnesota asset would be worse: no other retained Minnesota asset is the fee-waiver affidavit. FEE103 is its supplemental companion, not a substitute. The class is what is wrong.

resolvedIdentity.officialTitleAgreesWithEditionNote: The edition and the queue both record 'Affidavit to Request Fee Waiver', which matches the form-face heading. Confirmed rather than corrected.
resolvedIdentity.issuerBasis: The footer of every page carries www.mncourts.gov/forms alongside the form number and revision. The queue records issuingAuthority as null; the artifact supplies it.
resolvedIdentity.statutoryBasisNote: Printed directly beneath the heading. § 563.01 is Minnesota's in forma pauperis provision, which is what makes this a fee-waiver instrument rather than a generic supporting affidavit.
resolvedIdentity.scopeBasis: A Minnesota Judicial Branch statewide form published at mncourts.gov/forms and printed 'State' in its own footer language block, distinguishing it from any county edition. Not inferred from a service address.
resolvedIdentity.printedRevisionFooter: FEE102   State   Eng   Rev 07/24   www.mncourts.gov/forms   Page 1 of 6
resolvedIdentity.printedRevisionFooterNote: The footer repeats on every page with the page number advancing through 'Page 6 of 6'. It also encodes the jurisdiction level ('State') and the language ('Eng'), which is how the statewide and English editions are distinguished from any variant.
resolvedIdentity.currentnessDetail: The queue records the currentness question as 'Confirm REV-2024-07 is still the issuer's current revision.' This job establishes what the retained copy IS, from its own printed footer, and cannot establish what the issuer publishes today because the assignment forbids downloading.
resolvedIdentity.bindingCorrectness: All three component bindings are correct as they stand. The document they name is the document they need. No rebinding is required or performed.

measuredStructure.digestAgreementWithAssetAudit: exact — the audit records presence=present, binaryPresent=true, hashState=match and status=manifested_supporting_process
measuredStructure.nonWidgetAnnotationDetail: Two non-widget annotations, consistent with the mncourts.gov links printed in the footer. Neither is a form control.
measuredStructure.fieldCountNote: The edition records field_count 0 and structural_class flat_pdf. Both are measured correct. Unusually for this programme there is no widget-versus-terminal denominator question here, because both counts are zero.
measuredStructure.rendererConsequence: A six-page flat PDF with zero form fields cannot be filled by an AcroForm renderer. Any implementation consuming it needs a coordinate overlay keyed on page geometry, or the participant completes it by hand. Recorded as an observation about the artifact; no lane is assigned.

editionReclassRequired.whyTheGateRefuses: The authority gate treats supporting_process as unable to back an official-form component. It is refusing on a true rule applied to a class the artifact does not fit.
evidenceThatTheClassIsWrong: The document is a participant-completed affidavit filed to obtain a statutory remedy — waiver of filing fees under Minn. Stat. § 563.01 — not an ancillary process artifact.
It is the instrument by which the participant asks the court to act, which is the same shape as any other official form a packet delivers.
The Minnesota Judicial Branch publishes it in its own numbered form series alongside the expungement forms EXP101 through EXP106, not as guidance or process material.

Its companion FEE103, the Supplemental Affidavit to Request Fee Waiver, carries the identical supporting_process class and the identical defect, so this is a family-level classification rather than a one-row slip.
editionReclassRequired.precedent: The same defect and the same remedy were established for the Montana CRISS Expungement/Removal Request Form in an earlier wave: a participant-completed request form classed supporting_process, producing five role mismatches, correctable only by reclassifying in a successor edition rather than by remapping. Minnesota is the second instance, which suggests the classifier rather than the row.

correctionForTheSuccessorEdition.item: Reclass FEE102 from supporting_process to a class that can back a fee_waiver component
correctionForTheSuccessorEdition.to: a packet-form class with a fee_waiver document role, with the canonical path regenerated accordingly

queueContradictions.measured: The repository asset audit carries a full row for artifactId fee102-affidavit-to-request-fee-waiver-rev-2024-07 with presence=present, binaryPresent=true, hashState=match and an exact libraryRow reference to MN:FEE102:AFFIDAVIT:EN.
queueContradictions.resolution: The queue's statement is wrong on its face. A registry row exists and matches. This is a variant of the same conflation recorded across several other jurisdictions in this programme, where a queue field asserts absence for an asset that is present and adopted.
queueContradictions.correctionOwner: the queue owner; the queue is not this job's to write

queueContradictions.queueSays: Re-manifest the source under the document role the component requires, or map the component to the asset that carries that role.
queueContradictions.assessment: The first limb is right and is what this record recommends. The second limb is not available: no other retained Minnesota asset carries the fee_waiver role, so there is nothing to map to. Recorded so a later worker does not spend effort searching for the alternative the queue implies exists.

queueContradictions.measured: Minnesota Judicial Branch, from the mncourts.gov footer printed on every page.

revisionEvidenceComparatorArtefact.observation: The repository asset audit records revisionEvidence='differs' for FEE102, comparing repositoryRevisionText 'FEE102 State Eng Rev 07/24' against libraryRow revision 'REV-2024-07'.
revisionEvidenceComparatorArtefact.assessment: Those express the same revision in two notations. The recorded text is the full footer line including the jurisdiction level and language codes, not a bare revision token, so a substring comparison against REV-YYYY-MM cannot match.
revisionEvidenceComparatorArtefact.sameArtefactElsewhere: The identical pattern was recorded for Michigan MC-227B, comparing 'MC 227b Rev. 7/24' against 'REV-2024-07'. FEE103 carries it too, with 'FEE103 State Eng Rev 07/24'. It is a comparator behaviour, not a data defect.
revisionEvidenceComparatorArtefact.recommendation: Normalise MM/YY against REV-YYYY-MM, and extract the revision token from the footer rather than comparing the whole footer line, before treating 'differs' as a real discrepancy anywhere it appears.

doNotSubstitute.document: FEE103, Supplemental Affidavit to Request Fee Waiver
doNotSubstitute.why: The matched companion at the same revision and the same wrong class. It is supplemental to FEE102, not a replacement for it, and it is two pages against six. Binding it in place of FEE102 would deliver a supplement without the affidavit it supplements.
A Minnesota expungement form in the same retained set with a certificate-of-service role. Adjacent in the EXP series, unrelated to fees.

The Minnesota expungement instructions, petition and two proposed orders. All retained, all source_gated at REV-UNKNOWN, and none is a fee-waiver instrument. EXP102 is the petition the fee waiver accompanies, not the waiver.

doNotSubstitute.documentClass: a county in forma pauperis form
doNotSubstitute.why: The retained form prints 'State' in its own footer, which is the Judicial Branch's own marker distinguishing the statewide edition. A county form is not this document and must not be promoted to statewide.

doNotSubstitute.documentClass: the Spanish, Hmong or Somali editions of EXP101
doNotSubstitute.why: Retained language editions of the instructions, present in the same Minnesota set. A language edition is not a revision and none of them is a fee-waiver form.

sourceMaterializationEligibility.laterMaterializationPermittedDetail: Not while the class is wrong. Materializing FEE102 under supporting_process would carry the role mismatch into the runtime contract for three tracks, and the canonical path that encodes the wrong class would be pinned with it.
prerequisitesInOrder: 1. Reclass FEE102, and FEE103 with it, in the successor edition and regenerate their canonical paths.
2. Confirm REV-2024-07 against the Minnesota Judicial Branch by whoever is authorized to fetch.
4. Author a receipt pinning sha256 b8415cdd…c72da8 at 268,092 bytes with a destination under official-pdf/MN/.
5. Seal the materialized file at 0444 with every containing directory at 0555.

implementationFamilyEffect.effectOfThisJob: This job is one of two open dependencies of rcap-mn-flat-pdf-overlay, which covers three Minnesota tracks; the other is the Minnesota automation-blocked download job, which requires attended retrieval and is outside this session's scope. Resolving the class question removes one of the two reasons that job cannot be scheduled and identifies the correction precisely. It does not release the job on its own.
implementationFamilyEffect.familyReadinessStatement: The Minnesota official-PDF family remains fail-closed and this job does not move it. FEE102 stays supporting_process with runtime disabled, its currentness is unconfirmed, its licensing is unresolved, the five EXP-series assets remain source_gated at REV-UNKNOWN behind an attended-retrieval block, and no field map is built. No packet becomes generatable and no renderer is assigned.
implementationFamilyEffect.rendererObservation: A six-page flat PDF with zero fields is the coordinate_overlay shape rather than the acroform_fill shape, which is consistent with the family's flat_pdf_overlay implementation job. An observation about the artifact; the lane is not assigned here.

terminalDispositionDetail.why: The narrowest disposition the evidence supports. It is not unresolved_identity: the document, issuer, title, statutory basis, role, scope, revision and structure are all established from the artifact. It is not acquisition_required: the binary is retained and digest-matched to the adopted edition. It is not component_remap_required, which is what the parent job family would ordinarily produce — the three bindings are already correct and the defect is above them, in the edition's class field.

expectedDownstreamEffect: The Minnesota fee-waiver affidavit is confirmed present, correctly titled, correctly bound and structurally accurate in the adopted edition, and its three authority role mismatches resolve to a single asset-class error with a named correction and no new bytes. Three queue fields are identified as wrong, including one asserting no registry row for an asset the audit records as matched. The issuer, absent from the queue, is supplied from the form's own footer. A revision-comparator artefact is recorded for the third time in this programme with a concrete normalisation recommendation. One of two open dependencies of the Minnesota overlay job is answered. No component is rebound, no receipt is created, no binary enters version control, no renderer is assigned, no memo is edited, no edition is published, no packet becomes generatable, no runtime is enabled and no track changes promotion state.
